Case Reason 1 of 12
Payroll Reversal
Correcting a payroll after wages and tax debits have already been initiated. This action cannot be undone — always ask the right questions before proceeding.
Cancel vs. Reverse — What's the Difference?
CancelReverse
When to useBefore debits are initiated (before 4pm CT / NACHA not yet created)After debits have been initiated
What happensOriginal payroll deleted from Panda; data saved for admin to correct; cancels for ALL employeesOriginal stays on backend; new "reversed" payroll created; can target all OR select employees
Who can do itAdmin can cancel in-app — encourage them to do so if possibleGustie in Panda, or admin in-app (as of 2023)
💡
If an admin can cancel their own payroll, always encourage them to take that action on their account first.
Before Reversing — Ask These 4 Questions

⏰ WHEN are we reversing?

Before check date: Fine to pull funds.
After check date, <5 days: Can still pull funds.
>5 days after check date: Cannot legally pull funds (but can still reverse the payroll).

👤 WHO are we reversing?

Confirm employee names. Can reverse the entire payroll OR just select employees. You must reverse the entire paycheck — not just the overpaid portion.

📋 WHAT are we reversing?

Net Pay & Taxes: Full reversal — pulls back wages and tax reporting entirely.
Just Net Pay: Convert to check — changes payment method from DD to check.

📊 Guideline 401(k)?

Before check date: Reverse without looping in Guideline.
After check date: Must email Guideline at clients@guideline.com.
Two Types of Reversals

Full Payroll Reversal

Pulls back wages + taxes entirely. Use when a mistake was made — wrong amount paid, wrong employee, wrong quarter. Must reverse the entire paycheck (can't reverse just part of it).

Convert to Check

Changes payment method from direct deposit to check. Use after a bank error is received by Gusto — never in anticipation of a bank error. Wages are still reported; just the payment delivery changes.
⚠️
Bank error rule: Never reverse a payroll because a bank error is anticipated. Let the bank error play out — Gusto receives the error code in 2–3 business days and the system handles it. Acting prematurely creates unnecessary delays.
Running a Reversal in Panda (7 Steps)
  • 1
    Go to "Most Recent Payrolls" and select the check date you are reversing
  • 2
    Click Actions dropdown → Select "Reverse Payroll"
  • 3
    Select "Reverse Entire Payroll" OR select specific employees
  • 4
    Choose whether to select "Pull Employee Funds" (requires admin's written consent; NACHA takes 5 business days)
  • 5
    Leave notes — include the case number and reason for reversal
  • 6
    Click "Create Payroll Reversal"
  • 7
    Approve the reversal — must be done the same day!
Tax & Wage Implications
⚠️
Never promise the customer that: (1) wages will never be deposited into the employee's account, or (2) Gusto can guarantee recovery of funds already paid. We only have one attempt to pull funds — if that fails due to a bank error, the company must work with the employee directly.
Tax StatusWhat it meansWhat happens
PendingTax has NOT been sent to the agency yetReversing will refund the tax amount in a few business days. Verify deposit schedule — liability status is delayed by a day.
PaidTax HAS been sent to the agencyReversing will NOT refund. Company waits until end of quarter (or year for FUTA) when agency sees overpayment.
Reversals in closed quarters automatically flag for amended returns. If in a prior year, the system generates a W-2c within 24–48 hours.
Reversing Contractor Payments (4 Steps)
  • 1
    Open the check date → Actions menu → "Reverse Contractor Payment"
  • 2
    Enter a reason, select "Pull Funds," click "Create Contractor Payment Reversal"
  • 3
    No additional approval needed — but thoroughly check all details before clicking "Process Contractor Payment Reversal"
  • 4
    Leave a comment with your case number, WHY the reversal occurred, and WHO was reversed

Case Reason 2 of 12
Auto Wage Correction (AWC)
A system-generated correction tool that recalculates taxes for a specific time period based on updated information — without requiring manual entry.
What is it?
An Auto Wage Correction (AWC) is a payroll correction tool Gusties run in Panda to recalculate taxes after something changes — like a backdated address, a tax exemption update, or a risk class code correction. The system does the math; you review and submit.
⚠️
Before running any AWC: Always screenshot the current tax summary first. This lets you predict the outcome and catch unexpected changes before they happen.
When do you use it?

🏠 Backdated Address Change

An employee's home or work address was updated retroactively, changing which local/state taxes apply.

🛡️ Tax Exemption Changes

A company or employee-level tax exemption was added or removed for a past period.

🏗️ Risk Class Code Correction

A WA or WY workers' comp risk class code was wrong and needs to be corrected for past payrolls.
The 3-Step Process
  • 1
    Prepare Take a screenshot of the tax summary. Check the debit/agent payment summary to predict whether the correction will result in a debit or refund. Set clear expectations with the customer before running.
    • Confirm all settings in Panda are correct first (RCC, exemptions, address, rates)
    • Determine if the correction falls in a current or closed quarter
    • Check the company's Join Date to confirm Gusto can file for those quarters
  • 2
    Run the AWC In Panda → Employee Payrolls → Actions → "Run Auto Wage Correction Payroll."
    • Select the beginning and end dates (must be within the same quarter)
    • Current quarter: use the last actual check date in the quarter
    • Monthly filers: use the last day of the month, not the last day of the quarter
    • Do not check "Pay Employee State & Federal Withholding taxes" — employees reconcile on their own tax return
    • Click "Preview Wage Correction"
  • 3
    Review & Submit The preview shows original vs. corrected amounts, subject wages, gross subject wages, and impacted taxes.
    • Review carefully — incorrect taxes can sometimes appear, or a tax may be missing
    • Leave a detailed comment with your case number
    • Click "Run Wage Correction" only when the preview looks correct
Tax Implications

✅ Underpaid Taxes

The company owes more than was collected. A debit will happen the day after the AWC runs. Check the payroll debit date.

💰 Overpaid Taxes

More was collected than owed. Whether Gusto can refund depends on whether the quarter is open or closed and whether taxes have already been remitted to the agency.
Quarter StatusTaxes NOT yet paidTaxes ALREADY paid
Current QuarterSet taxes to pending in Panda — refund in 3–5 business daysGusto will request refund amounts in the original return at end of quarter
Closed QuarterFile a Payments JIRA (manual NACHA) if AWC didn't auto-trigger a refundCustomer must wait for amended return process — agencies send refund to company (not employee); takes 12–16 weeks (MasterTax) or 6 weeks (Pufferfish)
🚫
Gusto can only debit/remit taxes if: the company was with Gusto during that quarter AND Gusto submitted original filings. Check the company's Join Date. If filings show as "Rejected," corrections cannot be re-filed.
Key Terms
Subject Wages
Wages subject to a specific tax; YTD should never exceed the wage base limit.
Gross Subject Wages
Total taxable wages for this tax — reflects benefits/imputed income; will not reflect wage base limits.
Gross Wages
Total wages earned — usually matches the paystub salary.
SW vs. GSW
The AWC preview shows both Subject Wages (SW) and Gross Subject Wages (GSW) — both should shift after a correction.
Pufferfish
Gusto's internal tax filing system. Speaks directly to Panda. Covers IRS, CA, OH WH, NY, IL.
MasterTax
Third-party filing system Gusto uses. Does NOT speak to Panda directly. Amendment processing is slower (12–16 weeks).

Case Reason 3 of 12
Exempt Taxes
Managing tax exemptions at the company or employee level — and knowing when to use the CFIP Blocker tool instead.
What is it?
A tax exemption removes the obligation to collect or remit a specific tax for a company or employee. Exemptions may apply to federal, state, or local taxes and are usually granted based on legal status (e.g., nonprofit, religious org, realtor). Gusto supports two levels: company-wide exemptions and employee-level exemptions.
🚫
We cannot advise on whether a company qualifies for a tax exemption. Always direct the customer to their CPA or tax advisor. Our role is to implement what they tell us.
Company-Wide vs. Employee-Level Exemptions
TypeWhat it doesWho handles itExamples
Company-WideApplies the exemption to all employees at the company levelAdmin self-serves in Gusto app (Taxes & Compliance → Tax Setup)Nonprofit SUI exemption, religious org exemptions
Employee-LevelApplies the exemption to one specific employeeAdmin self-serves on employee's profile (Pay tab)Employee FICA exemptions, student FICA, minister housing
Setting Customer Expectations
  • Direct customers to their CPA or tax advisor to confirm eligibility before making any changes
  • Company-wide exemptions are self-served by the admin — walk them through where to find it
  • Employee-level exemptions are also self-served — direct them to the employee's Pay tab
  • After an exemption is added or removed, an AWC must be run to correct past payrolls
  • Exemption changes in past quarters require an AWC first, then a tax recon
Common Examples

📌 MA Unemployment Exemption

Some nonprofits or religious orgs are exempt from MA SUI. Admin configures at the company level. After adding, run an AWC to back-correct.

📌 TX Unemployment — Realtors

Real estate agents who are independent contractors may be exempt from TX SUI. Confirm with the customer's attorney before applying.

📌 WA FMLI CFIP Blocker

When a company improperly uses a company-wide exemption to stop $0 filings — use the CFIP Blocker tool instead.
Blocking $0 Tax Filings — The CFIP Blocker Tool
⚠️
Common mistake: Admins sometimes add a company-wide exemption just to stop $0 filings. This is incorrect — it can affect all employees and cause compliance issues.
The correct solution is the Internal CFIP Blocker Tool. Here's how it works:
  • 1
    Identify the problem — Company has been using a tax exemption just to prevent $0 filings, not because they are genuinely exempt.
  • 2
    Remove the incorrect exemption — Work with the admin to remove the improperly applied exemption.
  • 3
    Apply the CFIP Blocker — Use the Internal Filing Blocker Tool (IKB: Tax Process: Blocking $0 Filings). This blocks the specific filing, creates a $0 draft, and auto-restarts if the employer re-hires.
ℹ️
The CFIP Blocker automatically creates $0 draft filings so nothing falls through the cracks. If the employer rehires employees, the blocker reactivates automatically.

Case Reason 4 of 12
Non-Gusto Payroll (External Providers)
Entering historical payroll data from a previous provider when a customer switches to Gusto mid-year.
What is it?
When a customer switches to Gusto mid-year, Gusto needs their Year-to-Date (YTD) payroll data from their previous provider to ensure accurate tax calculations and filings. This is called entering a Non-Gusto Payroll (also called a historical or external payroll). The data must be imported as a spreadsheet — not a PDF.
🚫
Never try to import a PDF. PDFs cannot be used for data integration. Always request the report in .XLSX, .XLS, or .CSV format. Entering data manually from a PDF creates errors and downstream notices.
Before You Start
  • Install Microsoft Excel via Managed Software Center (sign in with firstname.lastname@gusto.com / Okta password)
  • Always check the Provider Playbook first — steps change and the Playbook has the most current instructions
  • Confirm which payroll provider the customer was using
  • Request the correct report format from the customer (provider-specific)
Provider-Specific Report Requests
ProviderReport to RequestFormat
ADP RunPayroll Detail Report (filtered by quarter)Excel-New download
QuickBooks Desktop (QBD)Payroll Summary (customized — remove Hours & Rates, export per quarter).CSV
QuickBooks Online (QBO)Payroll Summary By Employee (under Migration Documents/Reports)Excel (.XLSX)
PaychexDepartment Summary Data with Employee Detail (via Analytics & Reports → Live Reports).XLSX or .XLS
ZenefitsAll-in-One Report (Payroll → Reports & Forms → All-in-One) for the full date range.XLSX, .XLS, or .CSV
Formatting the Data (Gustie Steps)

After receiving the file, most providers' exports need to be reformatted before importing. The standard steps for QBD and QBO:

  • 1
    Open Excel and copy the text-only data (including column and row headers)
  • 2
    In a new sheet, right-click and select Paste Special → Transpose
  • 3
    Use Find & Replace: Find - (minus sign), Replace with nothing — this converts negative numbers to positive
  • 4
    Select all records, expand column widths, apply sort filters
  • 5
    Remove any blank entries before importing

Case Reason 6 of 12
Tax Reconciliation Payroll (Recon)
Running tax recons to collect or refund money after key events — keeping taxes current and preventing downstream errors like failed filings and agency notices.
What is a tax recon?
A tax reconciliation payroll ("recon") looks at total subject wages and associated tax rates, then calculates what taxes should be. If collected taxes are above or below that corrected amount, Gusto debits or credits the company's bank account. There are two types: automatic quarterly recons and Gustie-triggered recons after key events.
🚨
Recons are VERY important. Skipping or delaying a recon after a key event causes downstream errors — agency notices, failed filings, and delayed corrections. Always run one promptly, even if the corrections look unfamiliar.
What do recons correct?

✅ Recons DO correct:

  • Social Security (both portions)
  • Medicare & Additional Medicare (both)
  • FUTA (employer) & FUTA adjustments
  • State Unemployment & surcharges (ER)
  • SUI for NJ and PA (employee)
  • PFL for NJ, CT, DC, MA, WA (EE)
  • NM Workers Comp, VT Health Tax, WY Workers Comp
  • NY MCTMT, NV MBT
  • Local: Denver OPT, MA EMAC, OR Eugene CSPT, Jersey City Tax, Newark City Tax

❌ Recons do NOT correct:

  • Federal Withholding Tax (employee)
  • State Withholding Tax (employee)
  • AK State Unemployment (employee)
  • Everything else not listed (check the Reconciliation Payrolls IKB)
What events require a recon?

Run a recon directly after:

  • SUI rate changes
  • Adding or removing external payrolls
  • Benefit adjustments
  • Auto or manual wage corrections
  • Payroll reversals (closed quarters only)

Run AWC first, then recon:

  • Risk class code changes
  • Owner's Draw → Salaried/Hourly changes
  • Exemption changes (added or removed)
  • Courtesy withholding changes
  • Employee address changes
Running a Recon in Panda

Navigate to the company page in Panda → Operations → "Recons"

  • 1
    Select the debit date, year, and quarter
  • 2
    The draft recon runs first — review the preview before submitting
  • 3
    Check results: summary now shows breakdown by "Monthly" and "Quarterly" taxes, and separates "Taxes due to employee payroll" from "Taxes not attributable to individual employees"
  • 4
    Leave a comment explaining why the recon is being run (include case number)
  • 5
    Submit — customer emails are sent for any recon debit > $5
ℹ️
Bulk Recons: For running recons on multiple companies at once, use Taxes → "Bulk Recons" in Panda. Enter comma-separated company IDs or upload a file. Useful for batch corrections after a widespread rate change.

Case Reason 7 of 12
Workers' Comp — WA or WY
Correcting workers' compensation Risk Class Codes, rates, and account numbers for Washington and Wyoming — and running AWCs to fix mis-allocated taxes.
What is it?
Washington and Wyoming are monopolistic states — employers must purchase workers' comp from the state (not private insurers). Risk Class Codes (RCCs) categorize jobs by injury risk and determine the premium rate. When an RCC is wrong, missing, or carries incorrect rates, it causes payroll blockers, failed quarterly filings, and mis-allocated taxes.
Why corrections are needed

🔴 Incorrect RCC

The code assigned to one or more employees is the wrong code. Results in a payroll blocker ("Will block payroll in 7 days") and "Pending Company Suspension" in Panda.

⚠️ "Needs Attention" Warning

An RCC exists but has no rates associated with it. Admin must add rates via Taxes & Compliance → Tax Setup → Manage Taxes.

🔑 Missing Account Number

The state agency account number is incorrect or missing in the state field in Panda. This blocks Gusto from filing or paying correctly.

🔁 Wages Still on Old Code

An RCC was previously changed but wages/taxes from earlier payrolls are still tied to the old code. Requires AWC to reallocate.
Before Starting — What You Need from the Customer
  • The correct Risk Class Codes for each employee (available in their agency web portal)
  • The correct tax rates associated with each code
  • Confirmation that all employees are assigned to the correct code
  • The correct state agency account number
  • Written permission for Gusto to debit any missing taxes
Where to confirm codes

Pufferfish Employee Tax Summary

Shows all RCCs by payroll. After an AWC, the new code appears above the original. Each code has its own line.

Tax Code History in Panda

Shows each payroll's assigned codes by date — useful for confirming when a code change took effect.

In-App Compensation Section

Shows the employee's current RCC. Can edit in special circumstances by clicking "edit." Wyoming note: there are two RCC locations — both must match.
ℹ️
Past WA/WY employees (moved to another state): Their RCC won't show in-app. To access it: go to Panda → Address History → temporarily change to a WA/WY address → update the RCC in-app → restore the correct address.
Running the AWC for Workers' Comp

The AWC process is the same as standard AWC (Prepare → Run → Review & Submit), with these Workers' Comp-specific notes:

  • Ensure correct RCC and rates are saved in Panda before running
  • Current quarter: use the last actual check date; monthly filers: use last day of the month
  • After the AWC, check the wage correction payroll: positive amount = company owes employee; negative = employee owes company
  • Always run an auto-reconciliation payroll after the AWC to clear downstream tax calculations
  • Leave detailed comments on the quarterly filings page about all changes
⚠️
Gusto can only debit/file for quarters where: (1) the company was with Gusto during that quarter, AND (2) Gusto submitted original filings. Check the Join Date. If the original filing was "Rejected," corrections cannot be re-filed.
Removing an Invalid RCC (6 Steps)

Once wages/taxes are reallocated to the correct code, remove the old/invalid RCC:

  • 1
    Go to the company's Washington Tax Information section
  • 2
    Scroll to Workers' Compensation Rates
  • 3
    Click the most recent date for the RCC under the Effective Date column
  • 4
    Scroll down and click "Delete" next to the code you want to remove
  • 5
    Click "OK" to confirm
  • 6
    Refresh the page to confirm the code is removed
Marking for Amendment

Any changes affecting prior quarters require amended returns. To mark for amendment:

  • 1
    Click into the company's Quarterly Form Filing section
  • 2
    Select the quarter(s) that need to be amended
  • 3
    Leave a detailed comment with your case number explaining why the quarter is being amended
🚫
Gusto can only generate an amendment if we successfully filed the original filing. Double-check that filings were both generated AND successful in the Quarterly Form Filing section before proceeding.

Case Reason 8 of 12
FEIN Change
Handling Federal Employer Identification Number changes — from initial outreach through full migration, including employees, contractors, payroll, and benefits.
What is it?
A FEIN (Federal Employer Identification Number) is a unique 9-digit number assigned by the IRS to identify a business entity. A FEIN change is required when a company undergoes a significant legal change — like an ownership transfer, entity type change, or restructuring. This is a complex, multi-phase process involving migrating employees, contractors, payroll history, and benefits.
🚫
Not everything migrates. Benefits, some integrations, and historical payroll data may not transfer automatically. Set proper expectations with the customer before starting.
Who Needs a New FEIN?

✅ Needs new FEIN

Sole proprietorship → Corporation or Partnership; Corporation changes to another type; New partnership after change in partners

✅ May need new FEIN

Entity type changes (LLC → Corp, etc.); Ownership changes; Mergers and acquisitions

❌ Does NOT need new FEIN

Change in business name only; Change in business location; Adding employees
4-Phase Migration Timeline
  • 1
    Initial Outreach — Confirm FEIN change details. Use FEIN Changes IKB and Tier 2 FEIN Macros to set expectations. Determine if new Gusto account is needed (based on ownership change logic).
  • 2
    EE/CTR Migration — Migrate employees and contractors using the BOSS tool (EE/CTR migration). Handle NEXT Insurance transfer (9 steps). Move Guideline 401(k) before payroll migration.
  • 3
    Payroll Migration — Use the Payroll Migration Tool. All steps must happen on the same day. Determine contractor payment migration scope (full year vs. partial year).
  • 4
    Recap & Final Follow-Up — Cancel old account / turn off filing fees. Confirm FEIN Change in Panda. Run through final follow-ups checklist.
Key Rules & Watch-Outs
⚠️
Guideline 401(k) must be transferred BEFORE payroll migration. This cannot be reversed — if done out of order, it creates significant downstream issues.
ℹ️
Check for active GMB (Gusto-Managed Benefits) before starting. Route FEIN-Benefits cases separately for review.
💡
Payroll reversals after migration: If a payroll needs to be reversed after migration, use the Mass Payroll Reversal Tool — not the standard reversal flow.
What Can and Cannot Be Migrated
CAN migrateCANNOT migrate
Active employees (via BOSS)Historical wage data pre-Gusto
Contractors (via BOSS)Some benefits integrations
Guideline 401(k) (before payroll migration)Previous year W-2 history
NEXT Insurance (9-step process)Terminated employee records
Contractor payments (full or partial year)Previous tax filings/payments

Case Reason 9 of 12
Local Taxes
Understanding and correcting local tax codes — including geocoding overrides for Ohio and Pennsylvania jurisdictions.
What are local taxes?
Local taxes are taxes imposed by cities, counties, or special districts. They're calculated based on the employee's work address and/or home address. Local taxes are particularly complex in Ohio and Pennsylvania, where jurisdictions often overlap and geocoding determines which tax applies.
Key Tools

📍 Address Analysis (Panda)

Use this to verify what local taxes should apply based on the employee's address. First step when troubleshooting any local tax issue.

🔬 Symmetry (STE)

Gusto's tax engine that determines local tax rates based on geocoded addresses. Submit tickets here when rates/codes need to be updated.

🗺️ Geocode Override Tool

Used in Panda when STE agrees an address correction is needed. Re-geocodes all employees with that address.
Common Local Taxes by State

🏛️ Ohio Local Taxes

  • Municipal Income Tax
  • School District Income Tax
  • JEDD/JEDZ (Joint Economic Development Districts)

Use OH Tax Finder to verify correct jurisdiction.

🏛️ Pennsylvania Local Taxes

  • EIT (Earned Income Tax)
  • LST (Local Services Tax)
  • School District Income Tax
  • PSD Codes (Political Subdivision Codes)
  • HAB-PPT system

Use PA Address Lookup to verify PSD codes.

Geocode Override Process
  • 1
    Verify the address — Run Address Analysis in Panda. Check if the address is valid and what jurisdiction it maps to.
  • 2
    Submit a ticket to STE (Symmetry) — If the geocoding seems incorrect, submit a ticket to Symmetry support with the address details and the expected jurisdiction.
  • 3
    STE responds — two outcomes:
    • STE agrees: Use the address override tool in Panda to re-geocode all employees with that address.
    • STE disagrees: Use the admin override with a disclaimer. Use the Geocode Overrides tool. Use Google Maps for border research to support your case.
  • 4
    Check Build Kite / STE Logs — Review logs to confirm the change was applied correctly after the override.
ℹ️
Courtesy Withholding: Some states allow voluntary registration in an employee's home state. This is optional — the employer can choose to withhold for the employee's convenience even if not legally required.

Case Reason 10 of 12
Sales Tax Exempt
Processing sales tax exemptions for customers who qualify — using Gusto's third-party partner, Avalara, and the CertCapture portal.
Why does Gusto collect sales tax?
Following the South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018) Supreme Court ruling, online subscription services like Gusto are legally required to collect and remit sales tax in 22+ states and local jurisdictions. The rate (8.5–10%) is based on the company's filing address and is visible in Panda and on invoices.
🚫
We cannot advise on whether a company qualifies for a sales tax exemption. Common exemptions include nonprofits, religious/educational orgs, and resellers — but determination is up to the customer and their tax advisor.
Key Rules

🚫 No Refunds

Gusto cannot compliantly refund sales tax. It is the customer's responsibility to set up their exemption in the correct time frame.

🔗 Avalara Handles Validation

Gusto's third-party partner Avalara (via CertCapture) processes and validates all exemption documents. Avalara takes 3 business days to validate. If rejected, Avalara emails the customer directly.

👤 Customer Uploads Their Own Docs

Gusties never upload exemption documents for the customer. The customer must go through the CertCapture portal and upload their own documentation.
What to find in Panda

Go to the company's billing/payment plan details page → Tax Exemption Information:

  • Customer Code — Used by Avalara to identify this company. Needed when calling Avalara.
  • Certificates section — Shows all attempts, their status (pending/valid/invalid), signed date, expiration date, and jurisdiction.
  • Tax Exemption Request Form Link — The unique CertCapture link for this company. Send this to the customer.
  • "Generate new link" button — Use to create or regenerate the unique CertCapture link if needed.
Customer Workflow — CertCapture (7 Steps)
  • 1
    Customer opens the unique CertCapture link sent via email
  • 2
    Clicks "Add exemption certificate" to begin
  • 3
    Selects the exposure zone (state of filing address)
  • 4
    Selects the exemption reason (e.g., Charitable/Exempt Org)
  • 5
    Imports the exemption certificate and completes all required information fields
  • 6
    Electronically signs and authorizes the submission
  • 7
    Submits — Avalara validates within 3 business days
Calling Avalara
📞
Dedicated Gusto line: 206-826-2252. You can speak with the rep yourself or warm-transfer the customer. Identify the customer by Customer Code or company name.
  • Have Panda (Tax Exemption Information page) and Avalara's Customer page pulled up before calling
  • Avalara can explain why a document was invalidated and what documentation is needed based on the customer's nexus/exemption reason
  • Avalara cannot technically advise on whether a company qualifies — but they can guide on documentation
  • If you encounter issues requiring Avalara system access, reach out to your PE — they have access

Case Reason 11 of 12
Manual Wage Correction (MWC)
A last-resort tool that directly adjusts wages, taxes, and benefit amounts in historical payrolls. Use only when no other tool can fix the issue.
The Golden Rule
🚨
MWC is a LAST RESORT. It has no guardrails, is error-prone, and cannot be easily undone. Always exhaust every other option (AWC, Benefit Adjuster, standard corrections) before turning to MWC. PE approval is required for all MWCs except Minister Housing.
The Manual Wage Correction (MWC) tool in Panda directly changes wages, taxes, and benefit amounts on historical payrolls. Unlike AWC (which recalculates automatically), MWC requires you to calculate and enter every number manually — which is why triple-checking your work is essential.
When is MWC the right tool?

✅ Use MWC when:

No other tool can fix the issue; Custom post-tax deductions on historical payrolls; One-off tax situations (e.g., minister housing allowance)

❌ Do NOT use MWC when:

AWC can handle it; Benefit Adjuster can fix benefit amounts; The issue only affects the current open payroll
AWC vs. Benefit Adjuster vs. MWC
ToolWhat it doesGuardrails?PE Approval?
AWCRecalculates taxes automatically based on updated settingsYes — system-generatedNo
Benefit AdjusterCorrects benefit amounts (pre-tax/post-tax) without full wage correctionYesNo
MWCDirectly edits wages, taxes, benefit amounts — any field❌ NoneYes (except Minister Housing)
Pre-MWC Checklist (7 Steps)
  • 1
    Determine the exact issue — What is wrong, which employee(s), which pay periods?
  • 2
    Confirm no other tool can fix it — Have you tried AWC? Benefit Adjuster? Standard corrections?
  • 3
    Get PE approval — Submit to PE before touching anything. (Exception: Minister Housing)
  • 4
    Calculate all changes — Manually compute the correct wage, tax, and benefit amounts. Be exact.
  • 5
    Double-check your math — Have someone else verify your calculations if possible.
  • 6
    Check for debits/refunds — Will this result in a debit or a refund? Is the company aware? Do they have sufficient funds?
  • 7
    Set customer expectations — Communicate what will happen, when, and what the customer needs to do (e.g., issue a check to the employee).
Running the MWC in Panda (7 Steps)
  • 1
    Create a Wage Correction Payroll in Panda
  • 2
    Select "Manual Wage Correction"
  • 3
    Enter the check date and pay period
  • 4
    Adjust taxes, SW (Subject Wages), and GSW (Gross Subject Wages)
  • 5
    Double-check every field — Never drive wages negative
  • 6
    Create the Payroll Item
  • 7
    Send to PE for final review and submission
⚠️
Check Payroll Taxes Status: If taxes are Pending — Gusto hasn't remitted yet (refund possible). If taxes are Prepaid — Gusto has already remitted (no refund until amended return).
After the MWC
  • Run reconciliations (recons) after every MWC
  • Mark quarters for amendment if changes affect prior quarters
  • Leave detailed comments with case number on all modified payrolls
  • Inform customer of any debit/refund and what action is needed on their end
